item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Chris plans to order 24 issues of a magazine. He reads the following advertisements for two magazines. Ceds are the units of currency in Chris' country.

[Image: Advertisements for two magazines]

Which magazine is the least expensive for 24 issues? How much less expensive? Show your work.

descriptors: Teen Life. Calculations of both magazines are correct (60 ceds for Teen Life and 63 ceds for Teen News) and correct savings of 3 ceds
Other correct (e.g., Teen Life. Calculation of one magazine correct, the other not shown, and correct savings of 3 ceds).
Correct calculations (60 and 63 ceds), but incorrect or no magazine identified and/or no difference given
Correct calculation for Teen News (63 ceds), but incorrect calculation for Teen Life
Incorrect calculation for Teen News but correct calculation for Teen Life (60 ceds)
Teen Life, 3 ceds. No work shown
Other partially correct response (e.g., correct calculations but incorrect difference)
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

item.scoring_notes: Note: There is no distinction made between responses with or without units.

item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it.
